blocks.text: The tame ass has long ears (Kiduschin 33a); it is further distinguished from cattle by not being so broad-bellied, so broad-hoofed, so large-headed and so long-tailed as these (Chulin 60a). Its belly is as a rule white (Gittin 45a). With its hoof it can hollow out a considerable depression in the ground (Mikwaoth 5, 6), and the hoof, as with the horse, is often trimmed, since it is easily injured in milling, for which the ass was used. The ass namely went around in a circle to turn the millstone (M. Katan 10b). It can hold itself up for some time on its forelegs, but not, like the horse, on its hind legs (Sabim 4, 7; the opposite, but incorrect, statement [p. 141] is made in Sabbat 93a). It eats without much selectiveness, namely shrubs, thistles, etc. (ibid. 140b); out of hunger it once devoured a fish (B. Kama 19b), and since in eating it does not, like cattle, let saliva run off, the ox may eat the remainder of the fodder that the ass leaves, but the ass may not eat the remainder of the fodder left by cattle (Sabbat 141a). It was also customary to give it barley (Menachoth 69a). For a very young ass the fodder must first be ground up (Sabbat 155a). The ass brays as soon as the manger is empty (Temura 16a), yet the scrupulous gastronomy of a (genuine) ass is well known (Sabbat 112b); and on this, see §. 36 at the end.
The usefulness of this animal is manifold. People used to say: “The ox is created for the plough, the ass for carrying burdens” (A. Sara 5b); it was also used, as mentioned, for grinding grain.
Its urine is turbid and milk-coloured and is prescribed against jaundice (Bechoroth 7b); likewise the eating of its flesh is recommended against this disease (Joma 84a).

The barley found in its dung (Sabbat 110b), as well as the embryo in the body of a white she-ass, have healing power (ibid. 109b). Finally, the whip for convicts was made from straps of ass's and calf's leather (Maccoth 22b).
Its bite is more dangerous than that of the dog, for it breaks the bone of the one bitten (Pesachim 49b), and once it crushed the arm of a child (B. Kama 84a).

It used to bray at the end of the first night watch, i.e., at 10 o'clock at night (Berachoth 3a), and its braying is so loud that glass vessels were shattered by it (Kiduschin 24b). It is proverbial: “The ass is cold even in the middle of summer (בתקופת תמוז)” (Sabbat 53a), which is why a blanket is thrown over it, especially after the load has been taken off, so that it does not catch cold (Kelim 19, 3), and otherwise too it constantly wears a pack-saddle (בשטיל, Italian Basto, Sabbat 52b). For fastening the load a special instrument made of wood for this purpose was used (Kelim 23, 3). It bears the greatest resemblance to the mule (§. 168) (Kilajim 1, 6). Some fabulous statements about the ass have been given in §. 36. Finally, mention may be made of the Talmudic statement (Erachin 19a; but probably highly problematic) that the flesh of the ass has the specific gravity of human flesh, as well as of the statement (Bechoroth 19b) that the she-ass does not become pregnant before the third year of life.
If a pregnant [p. 142] woman steps on ass's blood, the children are said to become bald-headed or scabby (Ketuboth 60b).

The לובדקים, or לובדקם, occurring in Sabbat 51b and Kilajim 8, 4, is explained in various ways. Maimuni and Bartenoro on the latter passage say: This ass is found in לודים and resembles the camel (in size).
Maimuni on the former passage says: לובדקים are a kind of half-tamed ass and stand midway between the wild and the common ass.

Bartenoro on the same passage explains: An ass that comes from the land of לוד; it is stubborn and strong, so that it requires greater watching than the common ass. On the other hand, Raschi and the Tosephot on the first passage and Jeruschalmi on the last explain: “An ass that comes from לוב”; the Talmud itself calls it חמרא לובא (Sabbat ibid.) and in the pl. חמורים לובים (Bechoroth 6b); since לודים and לובים are not identical, לובים is in any case to be preferred. Commonly this word means Libya, a country in North Africa. Hitzig takes it (Jesaias p. 643) as Nubia, through confusion of ל and נ, and indeed in the Jeruschalmi (see Simson on Kilajim 8, 4) there is a reading ניבדקם; but we have no reason to abandon the twice-occurring reading לוב and לובים in the Babylonian Talmud, and we therefore translate with Münster: Asinus libycus “Libyan ass”, and not with Burdorf and others “Lydian ass”.

The Libyan ass is particularly suited for carrying burdens because of its size and strength (Bechoroth 5b), and because of its partial wildness it wears a breaking bridle (קיבצייל, Cheville, Sabbat 51b). In the Talmud this bridle is called פני דפרולא, which Schul. Aruch Orach Chajim §. 505, 1 explains by ברינה (Italian Freno).

In the Mishna (Kilajim 8, 4) it is ordained that the לובדקים may not be yoked together with camels. This ordinance does not necessarily presuppose a resemblance between the two animals, as is already evident from the same ordinance concerning the horse and cattle; nevertheless Maimuni, as mentioned, assumed a resemblance between the camel and the Libyan ass, which is probably to be understood as regards size, perhaps also colour. In any case the asses [p. 143] under discussion seem to be identical with the Asinis silvestribus, of which Pliny (h. n. 8, 30, 46) reports that Africa possesses a multitude of these asses. Some are accustomed to add the males of this species to their herds of asses; they are thus already half-tamed asses which are easily domesticated, and which, as mentioned above, are taken by some for our לוברוקים; one could therefore also translate לוברוקים as “forest ass”.
